items.title: Can you believe it? An investigation into the impact of retraction source credibility on the continued influence effect

judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect refers to the finding that people often continue to rely on misinformation in their reasoning even if the information has been retracted.
judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments, we found that source trustworthiness but not source expertise indeed influences retraction effectiveness
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico (dois experimentos) sobre o efeito de influência continuada, publicado em periódico revisado por pares dentro do período solicitado. O resumo não menciona temas proibidos (política, vacinas, COVID-19), estando alinhado ao recorte de neutralidade. O método e o achado principal descritos pelo usuário são condizentes com o conteúdo do resumo.

items.title: Does explaining the origins of misinformation improve the effectiveness of a given correction?

judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation often has a continuing influence on event-related reasoning... In two experiments, we examined whether a correction that explained misinformation as originating either from intentional deception or an unintentional error was more effective than a correction that only identified the misinformation as false... in a novel scenario with the same underlying structure.
judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments, we examined whether a correction that explained misinformation as originating either from intentional deception or an unintentional error was more effective than a correction that only identified the misinformation as false.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo experimental que investiga o efeito de influência continuada em cenários neutros (eventos), atendendo aos critérios de inclusão. O achado extraído reflete corretamente a conclusão do resumo de que explicar a origem da desinformação não aumenta a eficácia da correção.

items.title: Don’t believe them! Reducing misinformation influence through source discreditation

judge.evidence_topic: In two experiments, we tested whether immediate source discreditation could reduce people’s subsequent reliance on fictional event-related misinformation.
judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments, we tested whether immediate source discreditation could reduce people’s subsequent reliance on fictional event-related misinformation.
judge.reason: O artigo descreve dois experimentos com desinformação fictícia, o que atende aos critérios de neutralidade e empirismo. O achado principal extraído reflete precisamente o que está escrito no resumo.

items.title: Exploring factors that mitigate the continued influence of misinformation

judge.evidence_topic: Across three studies, we evaluated the relative contribution of three factors (i.e., targeting the misinformation, providing an alternative explanation, and relative importance of the misinformation content) to the reduction of the CIE.
judge.evidence_empirical: Across three studies, we evaluated the relative contribution of three factors (i.e., targeting the misinformation, providing an alternative explanation, and relative importance of the misinformation content) to the reduction of the CIE.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) por meio de três estudos experimentais, alinhando-se ao pedido. O resumo sustenta os achados relatados e não há menção a temas proibidos (política, saúde, vacinas, COVID-19), sendo o estudo focado na mecânica do CIE.

items.title: Vaccination against misinformation: The inoculation technique reduces the continued influence effect

judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect of misinformation (CIE) is a phenomenon in which certain information, although retracted and corrected, still has an impact on event reporting, reasoning, inference, and decisions.
judge.evidence_empirical: The main goal of this paper is to investigate to what extent this effect can be reduced using the procedure of inoculation and how it can be moderated by the reliability of corrections’ sources. The results show that the reliability of corrections’ sources did not affect their processing when participants were not inoculated.
judge.reason: O estudo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) e a técnica de inoculação, utilizando um desenho experimental. O achado principal está alinhado com o resumo, que confirma a redução da dependência da desinformação sob condições específicas de credibilidade da fonte e a relação entre crença na desinformação e dependência.

items.title: Examining the role of information integration in the continued influence effect using an event segmentation approach

judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation regarding the cause of an event often continues to influence an individual's event-related reasoning, even after they have received a retraction. This is known as the continued influence effect (CIE). Experiments 1 and 2 employed spatial event segmentation boundaries in an attempt to manipulate the ease with which a retraction can be integrated into a participant's mental event model.
judge.evidence_empirical: Experiments 1 and 2 employed spatial event segmentation boundaries in an attempt to manipulate the ease with which a retraction can be integrated into a participant's mental event model.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico experimental sobre o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) utilizando cenários de eventos neutros, atendendo aos critérios de inclusão. Os dados extraídos descrevem corretamente o método e os resultados apresentados no resumo.

items.title: Do the protective effects last? The effectiveness of alternative + forewarning/inoculation techniques in reducing misinformation reliance and reliance regression in the continued influence effect procedure

judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect (CIE) refers to continued reliance on misinformation, even after it has been retracted. ... In two experiments ( N = 441), we aimed to investigate the effectiveness of the alternative explanation technique and a combination of an alternative explanation and a forewarning (Experiment 1) or inoculation (Experiment 2)
judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments ( N = 441), we aimed to investigate the effectiveness of the alternative explanation technique and a combination of an alternative explanation and a forewarning (Experiment 1) or inoculation (Experiment 2)

items.title: How Stories in Memory Perpetuate the Continued Influence of False Information

judge.evidence_topic: The current work shows that the continued influence effect depends on the stories people have in memory: corrected misinformation was found to have a stronger effect on people's beliefs than information that was topically related to the story if it helped to provide a causal explanation of a story they had read previously.
judge.evidence_empirical: The current work shows that the continued influence effect depends on the stories people have in memory: corrected misinformation was found to have a stronger effect on people's beliefs than information that was topically related to the story if it helped to provide a causal explanation of a story they had read previously.
judge.reason: O artigo aborda o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) utilizando cenários fictícios (histórias), o que está em conformidade com o critério de neutralidade. O resumo descreve um estudo empírico ('The current work shows that...') e o achado principal está diretamente sustentado pelo trecho citado.

items.title: Can corrections spread misinformation to new audiences? Testing for the elusive familiarity backfire effect

judge.evidence_topic: This article presents three experiments (total N = 1718) investigating the possibility of familiarity backfire within the context of correcting novel misinformation claims
judge.evidence_empirical: This article presents three experiments (total N = 1718)
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada usando alegações novas (neutras), o que atende aos critérios de neutralidade e tema. O método experimental é adequado e o achado principal é sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Did he or didn’t he? Mixed evidence for the continued influence of retracted misinformation on person impressions

judge.evidence_topic: Here we report three experiments that tested for the continued influence of retracted misinformation on person impressions using a non-dynamic impression-formation task that is comparable to tasks used in event-related misinformation research. Participants formed an impression of a fictitious person based on a series of behaviour statements.
judge.evidence_empirical: Here we report three experiments that tested for the continued influence of retracted misinformation on person impressions
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico (três experimentos) publicado em 2025 que investiga o efeito de influência continuada com cenários fictícios neutros, atendendo aos critérios. Os dados extraídos estão corretos e condizentes com o resumo.

items.title: Does Mud Really Stick? No Evidence for Continued Influence of Misinformation on Newly Formed Person Impressions

judge.evidence_topic: Across four experiments, we investigated the impact of person-related misinformation and its correction on dynamic (moment-to-moment) impression formation. Participants formed an impression of a protagonist, “John”, based on a series of behaviour descriptions, including misinformation that was later retracted.
judge.evidence_empirical: Across four experiments, we investigated the impact of person-related misinformation and its correction on dynamic (moment-to-moment) impression formation.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico (quatro experimentos) publicado em 2024 que investiga o efeito de influência continuada usando cenários fictícios neutros (formação de impressão sobre um personagem), atendendo a todos os critérios do pedido. Os dados extraídos refletem corretamente o método e o achado principal do resumo.

items.title: The inhibitory impact of collaboration on the continued influence effect of misinformation

judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect (CIE) of misinformation refers to the persistence of misinformation's impact on memory and inference even when individuals are aware of a retraction. This study examined whether collaborative processes affect the CIE and investigated the underlying mechanisms through three experiments.
judge.evidence_empirical: This study examined whether collaborative processes affect the CIE and investigated the underlying mechanisms through three experiments.
judge.reason: O artigo é um estudo empírico (três experimentos) sobre o efeito de influência continuada (CIE), publicado em 2024. O resumo confirma o método e os achados extraídos. Não há menção a temas proibidos (política, saúde, vacinas, COVID-19), mantendo-se dentro do escopo solicitado.

items.title: Belief updating in the face of misinformation: The role of source reliability

judge.evidence_topic: This paper investigates the process of belief updating in the presence of contradictory and potentially misleading information... Our findings have broad implications for correcting misinformation in political, medical, and other applied contexts
judge.evidence_empirical: Across four experiments, we examined how individuals revise their beliefs when confronted with retracted information and varying source credibility.
judge.reason: O resumo confirma que o estudo é empírico (quatro experimentos) e investiga a atualização de crenças diante de informações retratadas, o que se enquadra no tema de efeito de influência continuada. Os achados extraídos refletem precisamente o que está descrito no resumo.

items.title: Comparing the use of open and closed questions for Web-based measures of the continued-influence effect

judge.evidence_topic: We compared the data quality obtained using open and closed response formats using the continued-influence effect (CIE), in which participants read a series of statements about an unfolding event, one of which is unambiguously corrected later.
judge.evidence_empirical: We implemented this basic procedure online (Exp. 1A, n = 78), comparing standard open-ended responses to an alternative procedure using closed-ended responses (Exp. 1B, n = 75). Finally, we replicated these findings in a larger preregistered study (Exps. 2A and 2B, n = 323).
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) utilizando cenários neutros (eventos fictícios), é um estudo empírico experimental com participantes humanos, publicado em 2018, e os achados extraídos são totalmente sustentados pelo resumo.
